This tension between precision and practicality appears throughout the legal disputes in relation to (1) identifying project beneficiaries and (2) quantifying project costs and benefits. Key lessons from transmission cost allocation legal disputes Overall, these cases indicate there is discretion in implementing cost allocation methods, provided these decisions are evidence based, cost and benefits are relatively balanced, costs are 5 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. assigned to project beneficiaries, and the analytic cost allocation methods roughly identify project beneficiaries. Courts have ruled benefits do not have to be calculated “to the last penny or, for that matter to the last million or ten million or perhaps hundred million dollars” for the purposes of cost allocation so long as there is more than “no benefits.” (U.S. Court of Appeals for 7th Circuit, August 2009). And regions do not have to use a particular formula as long as they can justify the method allocates costs “roughly commensurate” with the benefits received (U.S. Court of Appeals for D.C., August 2018). Emerging Cost Allocation Issues on the Horizon Growing interconnection requests from large loads may raise new cost allocation disputes. In November 2024, FERC rejected an amended interconnection service agreement in the PJM region that sought to facilitate a co-location arrangement between existing generation and a large load (PJM’s Susquehanna Co-Location Proposal 2024). In its ruling and a separate docket from a technical conference to address issues raised by this type of arrangement (FERC 2024b), FERC commissioners and participating panelists agreed large loads must pay their share of transmission costs, but there was disagreement as to what these costs entail and how they should be evaluated. As demand for data centers continues to grow, new methods may be needed to evaluate transmission cost responsibility from large loads. 1.2 Analysis Scope and Analytical Approach In this report, we evaluate what factors influence successful transmission cost allocation agreements.
